recipes.name: Taco Dip with Refried Beans
ingredients_raw: 0.5 head iceberg lettuce - rinsed, dried, and chopped

steps.text: Spread refried beans over the bottom of a 9x13-inch glass baking dish.
Mix sour cream and taco seasoning together until combined; spread mixture over beans. Top with a layer of salsa, followed by lettuce, tomatoes, onions, and olives. Sprinkle Cheddar over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Taco Dip with Refried Beans
raw_recipe.description: This taco dip with refried beans, spicy sour cream, salsa, tomatoes, lettuce, olives, and shredded cheese is always a hit at parties and potlucks.

review.reviewBody: I am rating this on the version that I made. This dip was wonderful, and one friend at the party I brought it to said that I was not allowed to bring the leftovers home. The only things I did differently was to put the sour cream on plain (no taco mix) and I made homemade guacomole that I put on top of the sour cream. So the layers went beans, sour cream, guacomole, salsa, veggies and cheese. I think the homemade guacomole really adds to this dip, and makes the use of the taco packet not really necessary, since you don't want too many competing flavors going on. Thanks for the recipe...I will use it often!!

The husband and kids inhaled this. I cut this recipe in half and made one extra layer with last night's taco meat (gets rid of leftovers and makes a yummy dip for the boys--win/win!) and I used green onions, reduced fat sour cream, homemade taco seasoning and homemade salsa. Huge hit. When I got back from coffee with the girls, it was gone. This was a snap to assemble in the morning and cover with foil before I left.

I did not use lettuce since it is supposed to be a "dip". I did buy a guacamole seasoning pack by McCormick and mixed with 3 ripe avocados along with about 3/4 cup sour cream. Mixed that up well and slathered it on top of the black olives. Then lots of Sharp cheddar cheese on top. The guacamole mix is spicier than I realized, but everyone seem to really like it. There wasn't any to take home!

Best taco dip I've ever had!! I also went with 2 cans of beans and yes you have to cut the lettuce very finely. Also, changing the layers to: beans, lettuce, salsa, sour cream, olives, cheese helped hold things together if you're worried about ease of dipping. Making it a little in advance will also allow the lettuce to absorb some liquid, which helps to make dipping easier. I added some coriander and cumin in addition to the taco seasoning, skipped the tomatoes and used extra salsa, and opted for low fat sour cream and cheese, then topped it with a few canned jalapeno slices. Yum.

This was super simple, fast and a hit with everyone. I added a guacamole layer on the beans and didn't bother adding fresh tomatoes since i figured there was enough in the salsa. I had green onions, so I used that instead of red. I probably used a bit less taco seasoning than suggested. 
I made a second dip without salsa for someone who couldn't eat tomatoes, but the flavour of the dip got kind of bland omitting it, so I would take that into consideration if you don't like tomatoes.

Made this taco dip many times, and it has been good every time. You may want to use less refried beans, maybe 2 cans instead of 3. You could also put the olives on top so people who dont want them can pick them off. Otherwise one of my favorite game day recipies!

The submitter of this recipe has requested that we change the amount of salsa listed in the ingredients from 1 (20 ounce) jar to 1/2 cup. She writes: "spread a thin layer of salsa over the beans, and then add the other ingredients." This will take care of the sogginess that some reviewers have noted! - The Staff

I made this for a carry in at work. It was a hit. 2 minor changes after Reading reviews I used only 2 cans of refried beans . I did drain the juice off the salsa to keep it from getting soupy. Otherwise I stuck with the original recipe. It goes great with taco seasoned hamburger and another girl brought taco seasoned crockpot chicken . Yum! Definitely going to be making it again and again.
I omitted the lettuce and added ground turkey taco meat. We also added jalapeños on top. I used plain sour cream since I was adding taco meat. I will definitely make this again. We all loved it.
A suggestion......I drain the salsa in a strainer to reduce liquid so not so soggy in dish. Great recipe !!
I have made this recipe many, many times for different functions and it is always a hit. I only use one can of refried beans though because I don't like the beans to overpower the dish.
It was Super good! took a bit longer than expected but was worth the wait.

We made this for my brother's graduation party last summer, and it was a delicious appetizer! We left out the olives, but included all of the other ingredients. I would highly recommend this for your next party or get-together!
Lots of compliments on this recipe! My only variation was adding some red pepper, and used two cans of refried beans.
I put a little more salsa . Yes I will make it again.
Big hit at a party. And easy to assemble.
